name: no_position_at_all
why: A book never opened has nothing to restore. This is the ONLY case that may yield an empty plan.

name: empty_record_has_no_anchor
why: A row that exists but holds no anchor is the same as no position.

name: current_hint_wins
why: A hint captured at the live anchor by this device is the most precise thing available.

name: stale_hint_is_skipped_not_fatal
why: The anchor moved after this hint was captured. It is ignored, and the anchor still resolves. Deleting it instead is what lost a real position.

name: locator_from_another_device_is_not_used
why: Readium locators encode how THAT device rendered the page.

name: cfi_from_another_web_client_is_usable
why: epub.js CFIs are derived from the EPUB DOM, so they are portable between browsers.

name: wrong_kind_hint_ignored
why: A browser cannot act on a Readium locator.

name: audio_moved_far_from_where_locator_was_captured
why: On an audiobook-source position the locator only describes the page if the audio has not moved on. The chapter is stale for exactly the same reason and by the same measure, so the audio rung — the one coordinate still current — is tried before it (issue #479). Dropping the hint but trusting the chapter is how a book opened hours from where it was being listened to.

name: audio_barely_moved_keeps_the_locator
why: Audio drift within the reuse threshold does not invalidate the page, so the hint still leads and nothing lossier is reached in practice. Behind it the audiobook ordering still applies (issue #479): the fallbacks are only consulted when the precise hint fails, which is when the page is least trustworthy.

name: web_written_position_seen_by_the_phone
why: The exact handoff that was broken: web writes chapter + preview + percent and no Readium locator. The phone must still land on the page, never at the start of the book.

position.epub_text_preview: althea counted the ships at anchor

name: percent_only_never_start
why: The invariant: an anchor exists, so the plan is never empty even with no hint, no preview and no chapter.

name: chapter_out_of_range_is_not_navigable
why: A chapter past the end of this spine cannot be opened; the percent rung still can.

name: zero_percent_is_not_an_anchor
why: 0% is indistinguishable from an unread book, so it must not masquerade as a position.

name: short_preview_is_not_searchable
why: Too little text to locate reliably; fall through rather than land somewhere arbitrary.

name: audio_only_position
why: An audiobook-only position still resolves to a page through the sync map.

name: listening_for_hours_with_a_stale_page
why: Taken from a real device (issue #479): four and a half hours into the audiobook, with the ebook coordinate still at chapter 1 and a preview left from the last time it was read. Only a reader save refreshes the ebook half, so it can be arbitrarily old while `source` says the audiobook is what is being consumed. Every ebook rung resolves — wrongly — so trying them first opened the book near the start, and the save that followed wrote that back over the real position. No case here covered a position whose two halves disagreed, which is why the ordering survived this long.

position.epub_text_preview: a running header that begins every file

name: chapter_zero_is_a_real_position
why: Chapter 0 is the first spine item, not a null. It must be navigable.

name: audiobook_hint_with_no_audio_anchor_cannot_prove_freshness
why: Issue #682: a Readium locator captured while reading, with no audio_position_ms stamped beside it, cannot be checked for drift at all — the check that would drop it never runs when there is nothing to measure. On an audiobook-sourced record the hint's freshness is unprovable, so it must not lead; the audio rung — the one coordinate known to be current — comes first instead, exactly as it would for a hint dropped by the drift check. A drive that stayed in one chapter (anchor_revision unchanged) used to leave the pre-drive page in charge of the reopen.

name: offline_local_row_with_no_audio_anchor_also_defers_to_audio
why: Issue #682's offline shape: a local row always reports anchor_revision 0 on both itself and its single hint (BookmarkEntity.toStoredPosition), so the ordinary staleness check never has a chance to fire either — the hint looks perpetually current. The same rule applies regardless: an audiobook-sourced record's hint with no audio anchor cannot lead, online or off.

name: ebook_hint_with_no_audio_anchor_still_leads
why: The new rule is scoped to an audiobook-sourced record. An ebook-sourced position has no listening session to have moved on without the hint knowing, so a hint with no audio anchor is exactly the ordinary case (most hints carry none) and must keep leading, same as before.
